name: Rosette-forming Glioneuronal Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic rosette-forming neurocytic cells with glial components on histopathological examination
MRI showing well-circumscribed, cystic and solid mass typically located in the fourth ventricle or cerebellum
Immunopositivity for neuronal markers (synaptophysin) and glial markers (GFAP) confirming mixed glioneuronal differentiation
Absence of IDH1/2 mutations and 1p/19q codeletion; possible PIK3CA mutations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of rosette-forming neurocytic cells with glial components plus supportive imaging and immunohistochemical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of radiological, histological, and immunohistochemical data.

pathognomonic.notes: Gait disturbance and coordination deficits due to tumor location
Headache caused by obstructive hydrocephalus from fourth ventricular mass effect

common.notes: Due to cranial nerve involvement or brainstem compression
Speech difficulties related to cerebellar involvement

occasional.notes: Involvement of cranial nerves V or VII
searchTerms: facial sensory loss or muscle weakness
tingling or weakness on one side of face

occasional.notes: Intention tremor associated with cerebellar lesions
Mild cognitive impairment secondary to tumor effects

rare.notes: Due to brainstem or cranial nerve compression
Rarely reported if tumor affects hypothalamic-pituitary axis

imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated cystic and solid mass in the fourth ventricle or cerebellum
T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense lesion with variable contrast enhancement
other: Histopathology demonstrating neurocytic rosettes and glial components
Immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin and GFAP

distinguishingFeatures: Ependymal rosettes rather than neurocytic rosettes

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
New onset seizures or focal neurological deficits
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC; 2021.
Kleinschmidt-DeMasters BK, Lillehei KO. Rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor of the fourth ventricle: a distinct clinicopathologic entity. Brain Pathol. 2002.
